title: The Day Stuffy Land Turned Inside-Out
subtitle: A strange storm unfolds the world in all the wrong directions.
editorialNote: New story adapted from a recovered plot summary; original wording was unavailable.

paragraphs: Opal woke to find the stars on the outside of the galaxy tent and the garden growing on the ceiling.
Langston hung upside down from a blanket loop.
“I meant to do this,” he said.
“No, you didn't,” Lolo replied.
“No. Please help.”
Coatl steadied the cushion tower while Opal and Axey untangled the blanket. Langston landed sitting down, with his breakfast bowl balanced perfectly on his head.
Outside, a river flowed through the air. Doors opened onto the rooms people had just left. A tree wore its roots like a curly hat.
An Inside-Out Storm turned above the village, pulling everything familiar into something strange.
Axey tried his compass. The needle pointed directly at his nose.
“Excellent. We have found me.”
Finley opened her notebook. Even her paw prints were backward. Stella leaned against her until she stopped looking quite so worried.
Opal wanted to fix everything immediately. She lifted her gemstone, but its light bent around the storm and returned to her hand.
“We need to understand it first,” Lolo said.
So they watched. The storm did not turn every place at once. It twisted only the things caught in the silver threads trailing from its middle.

illustration.alt: Opal holds her sloth lovey Lolo while reading inside the purple galaxy tent.

paragraphs: Water Kitty followed a thread along the floating river. Spirit Kitty sang softly, letting the moving air carry her notes around the tangled center. Coatl's buttons glowed as they approached a crooked archway at the village edge.
Beneath it stood a small weather keeper, clutching a map printed on both sides.
“I was trying to make a shortcut,” she said. “The road to my friend's house is so long. I folded the map until the two places touched.”
“And the world folded with it,” Opal said.
The weather keeper nodded miserably.
Langston looked at the root-hat tree. “A bold design decision.”
Opal wanted to say the keeper should have known better. Then she noticed the empty basket by her feet.
“Were you bringing something to your friend?”
“Soup. She hasn't been feeling well.”
Lolo crouched beside the basket. “You were trying to help. We still need to unfold the storm.”
Cinny studied the creases. There were three, each twisted in a different direction. Pulling all of them at once would tighten the knot.
They made a plan. The Dragon Couple carried two corners of the map together. Water Kitty guided the river gently down. Unique Pink marked each fold with a different ribbon so nobody would lose track.
The first fold opened, and the doors began leading into new rooms again.
The second fold stuck.
Langston offered to pull harder. Coatl shook his head.
“Sometimes strength means holding still.”
Langston held the arch steady instead. Opal followed the silver thread, finding a tiny corner tucked beneath the keeper's thumb.
“Here,” she said. “You don't have to hold it alone.”
The keeper let go. Axey eased out the corner, and Lolo helped her smooth it flat.
At the third fold, the whole storm shivered. Opal's gemstone lit the ribbons so everyone could move together. The last crease opened.
The garden settled to the ground. The stars returned inside the tent. Langston's bowl slid off his head.
“My crown,” he said sadly.
The weather keeper looked down the long road to her friend's house.
“The soup will be cold.”
“We can fill the pot with fresh soup,” Opal said. “And we'll walk with you.”

They took turns carrying the basket. The path was longer without a magical shortcut, but there was room for conversation, a rest beneath the trees, and a very detailed account of Langston's time as an upside-down king.
When they reached the house, the keeper's friend opened the door and smiled.
“You came.”
“We did,” the keeper said.
Lolo tucked herself close to Opal. Not every long way needed to be folded shorter.
The End.
